summary: Ayinapalli Aiyappan was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Madras. He served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960) and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1966–1970).

Ayu Khandro was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa. She taught A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé and Namkhai Norbu.
Ayush Maheshwari works in computational fields and Indology. He completed his PhD and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

Ayya Khema studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma (1978) and Sakyadhita (1987), and served as a teacher at Buddha-Haus in 1989.
Azizah Nur is a PhD student at the Australian National University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron (attested 2026).

B. Alan Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned a PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt. He taught at Rabten Choeling (1975–1979), lectured at UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001), and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies (2003).

B. N. Goswamy was an Indologist and historian who studied at Panjab University (~1952–1961). After serving in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958), he held a post at Panjab University from ~1965 to 1993.

B. N. K. Sharma studied at the University of Madras (BA, PhD) and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. He served as principal of Rajah's College (1938–1948) and later held professorships at Ramnarain Ruia College and D. G. Ruparel College (1953–1969).

B. R. Ambedkar studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, among other institutions, under scholars including John Dewey. He served as professor at Sydenham College (1918, 1920) and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai (1935).

B. R. Gopal was an Indologist and historian. He served as Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964), Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and Epigraphist at Epigraphia Carnatica (attested 1974).

B. R. Sharma is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as Assistant Director of Research at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005) and as a Scientist at the Arid Forest Research Institute in 2020.

Baatr Kitinov is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from Moscow State University. He has served as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1937–1938). He served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University (~1964–1968).

Baden Henry Baden-Powell was an Indologist and historian who studied at St Paul's School and the University of Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1889) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (~1882–1885).

Bahadur Chand Chhabra studied at University of the Punjab and Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953) and held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966) and Panjab University (~1965–1973).
Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1918) and held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu was an Indology and philosophy scholar who held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1948–1952), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1952), and the Institute of Philosophy at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).

Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist and historian who completed an M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai. An Indology and history scholar, he taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar studied at University of the Punjab, Heidelberg University, and under Mortimer Wheeler. In archaeology and Indology, he served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of CCRT (1982–1992).
